title: How To Be A Positive Leader

questions.q: What is a high-quality connection, as the book defines it?
a: An exchange that leaves both people more energized
A meeting that finishes with a clear action list
A friendship that lasts for many years
A conversation where one person mentors the other
questions.why: Lesson one describes these exchanges as ones where both people walk away feeling more energized.

questions.q: What simple habit does the book recommend for better connections?
a: Put away distractions and give the other person your full attention
Ask more questions than the other person does
Share your own stories to build rapport
Keep meetings short and focused on tasks
questions.why: Lesson one suggests silencing your phone, closing your laptop and truly listening when someone talks to you.

questions.q: What happened when university fundraisers spoke with a former scholarship recipient?
a: Their motivation and donations rose significantly
They asked for a higher salary
They began to doubt the cause
They spent more time on paperwork
questions.why: Lesson two cites a Michigan call center where meeting a student helped by their work boosted effort and results.

questions.q: Whom does the book say you should connect with to find meaning in your work?
a: The person who ultimately benefits from what you make
The manager who reviews your performance
The investor who funds your company
The colleague who shares your workload
questions.why: Lesson two says to find the end user, not just the buyer, and introduce your coworkers to them too.

questions.q: What question does the book suggest asking to test an ethical decision?
a: Would I accept it appearing on tomorrow's front page?
Would my closest friend approve of this?
Would this decision increase company profits?
Would anyone ever find out about this?
questions.why: Lesson three recommends imagining the consequences published in a major newspaper as a test of integrity.
